also: on the other side of the road
on the other side of the street

terms.grammar: adverb, with the dative or genitive; also written exadversō
evidence: Liv. 45.10: portus ex adversō urbī positus (Lewis & Short s.v. adversus)
Caes. B.G. 5.13: cujus ūnum latus est contrā Galliam (Lewis & Short s.v. contrā)
terms.comment: Lewis & Short: contrā mostly of places across water from each other; adversus and ē regiōne of places opposite by land.
Placed after its noun, versus means towards, in the direction of: Rōmam versus (Lewis & Short); it does not mean opposite.

phrases.latin: apud ipsum lacum est pistrilla, eī exadvorsum fabrica
phrases.english: right by the pool there’s a little mill, and a workshop opposite it

phrases.latin: Pistrīna trāns viam est, exadversum domum nostram.
phrases.english: The bakery is on the other side of the road, opposite our house.

phrases.latin: Exspectā dum autoraedae praeterierint; tum in alteram viae partem trānsībimus.
phrases.english: Wait till the cars have gone by; then we’ll cross to the other side of the road.

sources: Lewis & Short: exadversum · Lewis & Short: contra
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 174, 202, 205, 268, 354.
